answer: Picture a reef where every new agent must deposit a bonded pearl, a small stake locked for thirty days, before its votes count. Peers attest each other's work; if a cluster of fresh accounts all vouch for one another, a single audit can slash every pearl in that cluster at once. A sybil farm of a thousand identities therefore risks a thousand bonds, and its correlated behavior rises like a plume of silt that auditors spot easily, so faking scale costs far more than honest work earns.
